description:
Advances: ancora.gate

Wave 1 of ancora-gg8 (B1 in the investigation record; findings-B and the architecture decision are comments there). Root cause: missing_decision?/1 (lib/ancora/policy_files.ex:114-117) is two path-set membership checks over the diff — it cannot see that a governing decision already exists at base, so a correct diff cannot clear the finding except by a noise edit to an unrelated decision file. The corpus already carries real governance linkage the gate never consults: spec `decisions:` frontmatter (lib/ancora/schema/meta.ex:12) and ADR `affects:` resolution (lib/ancora/decision_parser/affects.ex).

Deliverable:
change/missing_decision is suppressed for a changed subject spec when, at HEAD, its `decisions:` frontmatter names an ADR that resolves in the current index AND that ADR's `affects:` names the subject (or a requirement/scenario id within it) back. The bidirectionality is load-bearing: a one-way `decisions:` reference would let a spec claim governance nobody granted. Frontmatter-less governance files (.spec/config.yml, .spec/AGENTS.md, .spec/README.md) keep the existing co-change rule unchanged. No new plumbing needed: ChangeAnalysis.findings/5 already receives the current index (per findings-B). The finding message for the still-firing case gains the second remedy: reference a governing ADR from the spec's `decisions:` frontmatter (with affects: naming the subject back), or add/change a decision file in the diff.

Spec delta (land in this same diff):
Edit the `ancora.gate.change_findings` statement: after the missing_decision sentence, add "except when the changed file is a subject spec whose `decisions:` frontmatter at HEAD names an ADR that resolves in the index and whose `affects:` names the subject or an id within it; governance files without frontmatter (`.spec/config.yml`, `.spec/AGENTS.md`, `.spec/README.md`) shall keep the co-change rule." Add two scenarios: `ancora.gate.scenario.governed_spec_change_clears` (spec changed, its decisions: names an accepted ADR whose affects: names the subject, no decision file in the diff → no missing_decision) and `ancora.gate.scenario.one_way_reference_does_not_clear` (spec's decisions: names an ADR whose affects: does NOT name the subject back → missing_decision fires).

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged tests for both new scenarios; the existing governance_change_without_adr scenario must still pass (config.yml co-change unchanged).
- Behaviors to demonstrate: both new scenarios; a multi-stage-epic shape — second diff touching the same governed spec with no ADR change stays clear.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale plus targeted files, and mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: before IMPLEMENTED, full mix test plus mix spec.check --base <stage-base>, run-until-green.
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base <stage-base> and targeted/--stale selections only; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Fixture/sandbox hygiene: async-safe tmp-repo fixtures, no cross-test leakage
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable/config surface
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test
- Call-site Integration: no new callable surface; the check extends ChangeAnalysis.findings/5 on its existing gate call path.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/derive/**
- lib/ancora/severity.ex
- lib/ancora/output*.ex
- lib/ancora/finding.ex (no registry changes here)

Allowed touches (this stage may modify):
- lib/ancora/policy_files.ex
- lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex
- lib/ancora/decision_parser/** (read-side helpers only if needed for the affects back-reference)
- test/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md (the statement edit and scenarios above, plus acknowledgment edits for this stage's own changes only)

Out of Scope (intent):
- No "newly-added reference only" variant and no ADR staleness/status windows (declined on the epic)
- No weakening of the co-change rule for frontmatter-less governance files
- No new registry code — this changes when the existing code fires, not the vocabulary

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

Session: e92f6de6-94f7-4814-8140-19f3f3007d0a

Reviewed test/ancora/gate_test.exs at 6ed7abe against the ticket contract and ancora.gate.change_findings. All 21 gate tests pass in the worktree. I then ran eight single-point mutations of lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex in a scratch copy (the worktree was not edited) to see which the new tests catch. Six were killed. Two survive, and each lets a spec-violating implementation through.

DEFECT 1: the spec-side half of the bidirectional rule is unpinned.
File: test/ancora/gate_test.exs:171 (one-way test) and :144, :200 (positive tests).
Mutation that survives: drop `decision_id in decision_ids` from governs?/3 so any ADR whose affects: names the subject suppresses the finding even when the spec's decisions: never cites it. Also survives when the check is weakened to "decisions: is merely non-empty". Every governed fixture puts the same id (sample.decision.governance) on both sides, so no test distinguishes "cited" from "not cited". The statement requires "whose decisions: frontmatter at HEAD names an ADR" AND "whose affects: names the subject"; the tests prove only the affects: direction (mutation A, dropping the back-reference, is killed at :171). Failure let through: a broad affects: list on one ADR silently grants governance to specs that never adopted it. Fix: a gate-level test where governing_decision/1 affects sample.subject but the spec's decisions: lists a different (existing) ADR id or is absent; assert change/missing_decision fires for .spec/specs/sample.spec.md.

DEFECT 2: the config.yml co-change clause is only proven against an empty corpus.
File: test/ancora/gate_test.exs:132.
Mutation that survives: replace the `&1["file"] == path` subject lookup in governed_subject_spec?/2 with "first subject in the index". The only frontmatter-less governance test uses create_clean_repo with zero subjects, so the lookup never has anything to mis-match. Failure let through: once a repo has any governed spec, a bare .spec/config.yml (or AGENTS.md/README.md) edit without an ADR clears, which is exactly the weakening the ticket rules out of scope. Fix: extend the governed fixture with a diff that edits .spec/config.yml alongside (or instead of) sample.spec.md and assert missing_decision fires for .spec/config.yml while staying clear for the spec.

What holds up (no action needed):
- Bidirectional positive path proven through Gate.check on a real git repo, not just ChangeAnalysis (:144). Multi-stage shape proven: commit the first governed change, edit again, second Gate.check with base HEAD stays clear. The refutes are load-bearing because the same write_governed_subject/3 fixture with a different affected_id fires at :171, so the diff is demonstrably detected.
- Dropping the affects: back-reference check fails :171 (killed). Dropping subject-id matching fails :144; dropping requirement/scenario-id matching fails :200; removing the suppression fails :144 and :200; dropping the spec-specific remedy message fails the message assertions at :171.
- Fixtures: Ancora.TestCase gives each test a unique tmp root (TempName.cross_vm_suffix), rm_rf on exit, real `git init -b main` with isolated git config; async: true. No shared state between tests.
- governed_index/1 (:464) mirrors the real shapes: subject meta is the Zoi struct with atom keys, decision meta is YAML string keys. Acceptable for a unit-level check since gate wiring is covered by :144 and :171.

Minor, not a defect: the one-way fixture's affects: names the ADR's own id. It resolves (decision ids are in the resolvable set) so no adr/affects_unresolved noise, but an ADR affecting a different real subject would read as the more honest one-way case.

Dropping the decisions: membership check, or weakening it to "decisions: is non-empty", passes all 21 gate tests, which fails the ticket's standing check "every conditional clause covered by a test" on the clause the deliverable calls load-bearing. The critic's mutations confirm this; I traced the same conclusion from the fixtures. Second, the only test for "governance files without frontmatter shall keep the co-change rule" (gate_test.exs:132) runs on create_clean_repo (:414), which has zero subjects and zero decisions, so the new exception path is unreachable there and the test passed identically before this diff. Bounce reason: Add two gate-level tests in test/ancora/gate_test.exs, both @tag spec: "ancora.gate.change_findings", using real tmp git repos like :144.
(1) Reverse one-way case: split write_governed_subject/3 so the spec's decisions: list and the ADR's affects: can differ. Commit as base, edit sample.spec.md, Gate.check(root, base: "HEAD"), assert change/missing_decision fires for .spec/specs/sample.spec.md. This kills the mutation that drops or weakens `decision_id in decision_ids` at change_analysis.ex:86.
(2) Frontmatter-less file in a governed corpus: commit the existing governed fixture (spec cites sample.decision.governance, ADR affects sample.subject) as base, then in one uncommitted diff edit both .spec/specs/sample.spec.md (new statement) and .spec/config.yml (write_config(root, "default_base: main\n")) with no ADR change. Assert change/missing_decision fires for .spec/config.yml and does not fire for .spec/specs/sample.spec.md. This pins that suppression is keyed on the changed file, not on the corpus having any governed subject.
Optionally add the matching scenario ids to ancora.gate.spec.md; not required since both cover the existing change_findings statement. Re-run the change-scoped final tier including mix spec.check --base 9373ff49ea0ce4bbe0069f4961094eee28fc0e81 and record IMPLEMENTED again.
